climb.rationale: Index of coincidence first, then the published n-gram counts, which is the ordering Ostwald and Weierud describe. Measured at 167 letters with ten pairs: n-grams alone from the identity plugboard recover the exact plugboard on 3 of 8 key draws; seeding with an index-of-coincidence climb recovers 8 of 8 for 1.6x the work.

positive_controls.rationale: The five independently solved 1941 Army plaintexts Phase 7 already uses, each kept as its own message with its own indicator and enciphered by enigma.EnigmaI under one shared ten-pair daily key. That is the real Army situation: several short messages under one key. An earlier version of this control concatenated the five into two messages at the target lengths and failed, because the junctions between unrelated messages are n-grams no Army text contains; the concatenated form was not a legitimate control and was replaced rather than reinterpreted.

key.plugboard: AV BS CG DL FU HZ IN KM OW RX

positive_controls.rationale: Three messages at exactly the target lengths 167, 107 and 97, from constructed Army-style text that cannot overlap the published n-gram counts. Trades authenticity for a guarantee of no training overlap, so the two controls fail in different ways if either weakness matters.

key.plugboard: AN BY CF DR GJ HS IL KM PV QZ

hypothesis: A climb that searches the position of one dropped or inserted letter (stecker_split.SplitClimber) detects at least 45% of the one-indel draws, with the indel in letters 56 to 111, that neither past-notch climb detects, where the complete ring rule detects 20.3% and an oracle that is handed the position 70.3% (phase1-middle-complete-power-v1), and at least 30% of the one-indel draws with the indel elsewhere that both miss, at about 2.9 times the cost of the windowed climb the completed sweep v3 used, against 9 times for the complete rule.
refuted_by: S1 below 45% or S2 below 30%, scored by scripts/split_power.py on strata of at least 25 draws (a smaller stratum is not estimable and refutes nothing). S3 to S6 and the runner's marginal predictions each refute only themselves.

end_to_end_power.rationale: phase1-middle-complete-power-v1 found that among planted keys neither past-notch climb detects, the complete ring rule recovers 20.3% of those with the indel in the middle third and an oracle that undoes the indel 70.3%, and its preregistered rule chose a split-point climb to be built and benchmarked. This run measures that climb on the same draws: the seed, key, plaintext, fault and slice are those of the control, so every draw is paired with the control's complete-rule and oracle outcomes, and the two past-notch arms are rerun as a replication check that the draws and the runner are the same. The complete arms and the oracle are not rerun; scripts/split_power.py takes them from the control's artifact and refuses to go on if any draw was planted differently. The split-point climb decrypts the head with keystroke i and the tail with keystroke i + 1 or i - 1 of the same setting, and searches the position of the fault inside every evaluation; its n-gram phase scores every position, its index-of-coincidence phase a grid of 32 letters.

predictions.statement: The whole-message past-notch arm detects at least 79.0% of unperturbed draws (316 of 400 in the control, and the same draws).
The W = 117 past-notch arm detects at least 42.5% of single-indel draws (170 of 400 in the control).
The split-point climb detects at least 70% of unperturbed draws; its null is inflated by the best of about 330 hypotheses, so this is the price of searching the position.
The split-point climb detects at least 60% of single-indel draws (the whole-message climb got 36.8%, W = 117 got 42.5%, the complete rule with W = 117 got 64.5%, the oracle 77.0%).

end_to_end_power.right_neighbours_rationale: The tail window decrypts cleanly only at the setting one keystroke away from the planted one (the right position one further for a deletion, one back for an insertion). A complete sweep enumerates every right position, so it always visits that setting; the slice includes the planted right position and both neighbours for every arm, so the whole-message arm is measured on the same slice as the windowed ones. v1 swept the planted right position only, so this whole-message arm is a re-measurement on a wider slice, not a replication of v1's number.
end_to_end_power.arm_rationale: past_notch_whole and past_notch_w117 are the control's reference arms, rerun to prove the draws and the runner are unchanged. oracle_past_notch is rerun so this artifact stands alone; it is the ceiling for any split-point climb. split is stecker_split.SplitClimber with the declared parameters: an index-of-coincidence grid of 32 letters, candidates processed 64 at a time (no effect on any number), and a credit of -8.66 per dropped n-gram term for a masked hypothesis.
end_to_end_power.sweep_decision_rule: A windowed sweep of BYQMZ is preregistered next only if windowed-117-indel-at-least-30pct, windowed-117-indel-gains-10-points and windowed-117-clean-loss-at-most-25-points all hold. It then uses W = 117 and states this run's W = 117 rates as its power. If they do not all hold, no windowed sweep is run on this evidence, whatever another window size measures; a different W would need its own calibration with a fresh seed.

split_analysis.status: The script is committed with this configuration and unit-tested on synthetic draws; it has not seen a result.

strata.clean: cell 0, missed by both reference arms
strata.indel_middle_third: cell 1, planted position 56 to 111 inclusive, missed

predictions.statement: The split-point climb detects at least 45% of the middle-third-indel draws both past-notch climbs miss (the control: complete rule 20.3%, oracle 70.3%, on 118 draws).
The split-point climb detects at least 30% of the elsewhere-indel draws both miss (the control: complete rule 44.6%, oracle 52.7%, on 74 draws).
The split-point climb detects at most 40% of the clean draws both miss (the complete rule's 59.6% there comes from ring coverage, which this climb does not change).

complete.source: settings ratio of the complete to the past-notch rule, 246.8 million over 27.4 million, applied to v3's windowed climb

split.source: scripts/benchmark_sweep.py --settings 6760 --jobs 10 --compare --split-grid 32 --repeats 2, 2026-10-06: split 10.44 ms/setting against windowed 3.62, interleaved, on this host; measured before this run and applied to v3's 16.95 h

yield_model.definition: As in phase1-middle-complete-power-v1: conditional detection probability given a standard reading and both completed sweeps null, divided by host-hours.
yield_model.weights: w_clean = (1 - q) * m_clean and w_indel = q * m_indel, m the fraction of that cell's draws missed by both reference arms, q the unmeasured prior of one indel.
yield_model.probability: (w_clean * a_clean + w_indel * a_indel) / (w_clean + w_indel), with a the arm's detection rate among the missed draws of that cell (the indel strata pooled).
yield_model.nominal_fault_prior_note: The value the control declared; arbitrary, and the rule's outcome at every other q is printed.

decision_rule.split_dropped: If S1 and S2 are both refuted, the split-point climb is dropped and the complete-rule sweep is preregistered.
decision_rule.otherwise: The sweep with the higher conditional detection per host-hour at the nominal q is preregistered next, with its measured rate as its stated power; the yields at every q are printed, and the either-candidate rate is exploratory.
decision_rule.not_decided_here: No sweep is run on this evidence. The sweep needs its own preregistration with a stated power and a checkpointed run.

pre_run_facts.disclosure: Everything below was known before this run and shaped the climb or the thresholds. None of it is a result on the control's draws.
pre_run_facts.development_draws: 60 planted 167-letter one-indel draws from seeds 1000 to 1059 of the test helper, not the control's seed, climbed at the true setting: split 39 of 60 (65%) against 14 of 60 for the whole-message climb and 16 of 60 for the W = 117 climb; with the indel in letters 56 to 111, 20 of 28 against 1 and 4; elsewhere 19 of 32 against 13 and 12. A true-setting rate bounds the stecker stage, not a sweep.
changes_after_looking_at_development_dra: the mask credit of -8.66 per dropped term, one term for a dropped letter and two for an inserted one, because without it a clean message was labelled as a fault near an end
an index-of-coincidence grid of 32 letters instead of 16 (39 of 60 either way, about 15% cheaper)
processing candidates 64 at a time, which changes no number and halves the cost under 10 workers
pre_run_facts.what_was_known_of_the_control: The control's artifact was public when the thresholds were set. S1 to S3 and the 70% and 60% marginals were chosen against its figures for the complete rule (20.3%, 44.6%, 59.6%) and the oracle (70.3%, 52.7%); the split-point climb itself was not run on any of the control's draws before this run.
pre_run_facts.benchmark: split 10.44, windowed 3.62 and whole-message 2.90 ms per setting, 6,760 settings, 10 workers, two interleaved rounds; before blocking the split climb ran 22.0 ms per setting.

run_constraint: Not run. Run from a clean tree on an idle host with --jobs 10, after this configuration and scripts/split_power.py are committed. Projected cost: 4 arms over 45 settings per draw, the split arm about 3 times a windowed climb per setting, plus null climbs, 800 draws; about 20 to 30 minutes on 10 workers. Then python3 scripts/split_power.py.
limitations: The slice is the planted key's own neighbourhood: the planted wheel order, left offsets within one of the planted, middle offsets within two, and the planted right wheel. Every other wheel order and distant start is absent, so a detection is a detection against that neighbourhood and a pooled wrong-setting null, not against 2.7e7 settings. The detection threshold is set at 6 null standard deviations to stand in for the extreme value of that many draws, and that substitution assumes the null is close to normal.

The right wheel's ring and position are taken at the planted values (or, for the AAA arm, at the planted right offset with ring A). That is the one axis the full sweep enumerates exactly, so it always visits those values, but the experiment does not test it.
One plaintext prefix at one length is used for every draw. The draws vary the key, not the text, so a text that scores unusually well or badly under the published counts moves every rate together.

The null is the climb's score at randomly drawn wrong settings of the same message. It is pooled over the cell's draws, eight per draw, and is a reference distribution rather than a sample of the space a sweep would see.

The indel cell drops or inserts one random letter at a uniformly random interior position. Real garbles can be several letters, can fall in the first or last few letters, or can be a transposition; this measures the single-letter case only.
Constructed plaintext enciphered by the reference machine, not authentic held-out traffic with an authentic daily key.

The right wheel's position is swept over the planted value and its two neighbours, so the slice holds the setting one keystroke away that the tail window needs. Under the middle-past-notch rule the middle wheel's phase is fixed, so when the planted machine's first keystroke steps its middle wheel the shifted setting is not exactly reachable; the measurement includes that loss rather than assuming it away.

Each windowed arm is compared with its own pooled null, the same windowed climb at the same wrong settings, because the better of two shorter windows is distributed differently from a whole-message score. The 6-sigma threshold stands in for the extreme of a full sweep in which every setting contributes the better of two windows, which is twice as many scores as the whole-message sweep and assumes the windowed null is also near normal.

'Missed by both past-notch arms' stands in for 'v2 and v3 both null'. The real sweeps compare a candidate against a score distribution over 27.4 million settings; this control compares against a pooled null of wrong settings, as every earlier power control did. The joint figures in phase1-body-direct-sweep-v3 (73 of 80 clean) were measured the same way.

The missed set is defined by outcomes on the same draws that then measure the complete arms, so a complete arm that fails for a reason the past-notch arms share (the same unlucky plugboard) is under-counted among the missed, and one that succeeds by retrying a different equivalent setting is over-counted. Neither effect is estimated.

400 draws per cell leave about 36 clean missed draws and about 100 middle-third indel missed draws, if the rates of the earlier controls hold. A rate in a stratum of 36 has a 95% interval about 0.3 wide. The thresholds are set with that in mind and the strata sizes are reported.

Only a single dropped or inserted letter is modelled, with the head-and-tail argument of phase1-windowed-climb-power-v1. Two faults, a substituted letter, or a fault in the first or last letters behave differently.

Every figure assumes UKW-B, wheels I-V as wired and the 1940+ indicator procedure. The cited paper's authors suspect Batch C used differently wired wheels; if so, no planted-key power here applies to it.

The split-point climb judges a hypothesis by an n-gram score from which the junction terms are dropped and a fixed credit added. The credit, -8.66 per term, is the wrong-setting null mean per letter measured in the control and applies to a message with masks of its own only approximately; BYQMZ carries one masked letter at position 28 and the planted draws carry none.

The split arm is judged against its own null, the same climb at the same wrong settings as the pooled null, because the best of about 330 hypotheses is distributed differently from a single score. The 6-sigma threshold assumes that null is near normal.
The oracle arm is judged against its own null, as amended in the control, and is the ceiling for any split-point climb: it is handed the fault's position and kind.
q, the prior probability of an indel, is not measured and the nominal 0.2 is arbitrary. The yields at every reported q are printed.
Only a single dropped or inserted letter is modelled. The split-point climb has one fault hypothesis; two faults are not searched.

The strata are defined on the same draws that score the split arm, as in the control, and the control's complete-rule and oracle outcomes come from a different run of the runner on the same seed; the script checks that every draw's planted key and fault are identical and counts any past-notch arm that does not reproduce.
